name: Richard Meshack Rotji
flagReason: Borderline-low score with genuinely strong remediation-by-effort and detection rows sitting on top of a fabricated spine (AWS metadata SSRF, IAM credentials, 84,210 records, 1.2M transactions). Worth a second look before elimination given the real craft in D3.
feedback: D1: You correctly caught the SQL injection in the login concat with the quoted SELECT line (A03/CWE-89), the stored XSS with the exact cookie beacon to 185.220.101.9:8443 (CWE-79), the XXE in 04-import-xxe.xml (CWE-611), and the JWT alg:none acceptance with Token2 (CWE-347). That is four of the ten real findings, so the catalogue is roughly a third complete, not six-of-six as the header claims. You missed the unsalted MD5 hashing (A02/CWE-916), the hardcoded JWT secret sankofa-legacy-admin-2019 (CWE-798), the missing token expiry (CWE-613), the path traversal at capture 02:24:02 reading /etc/passwd (CWE-22), the open redirect via ?next= in D1, and the cookie missing Secure and SameSite (CWE-614). Two of your entries are not in the pack at all: a reflected XSS in search and the whole SSRF-to-169.254.169.254 cloud metadata story with AccessKeyId and IAM role credentials. That AWS metadata chain, the 84,210 record figure, and the 1,203,940 transactions do not trace to any artefact; the only data quantity in the pack is the 312-row exfil sample, which you even cite correctly in one place and then contradict. I have to call that plainly: the cloud-credential SSRF and the 84,210 impact are invented evidence, so I scored the impact row zero and applied the fabrication penalty. The decoy was also missed; you labelled alg:none as 'not a decoy,' but alg:none is a live vulnerability, and the safe construct you needed to name and prove sound is the HS256 verify branch using hash_equals(), which is constant-time, so timing attacks on that branch fail. D2: The chain hops you did reconcile are right and verbatim, SQLi at 02:15:31, stored XSS at 02:18:47, open redirect at 02:21:13, and the PoC bodies match the capture cleanly, which is good work. The problem is the spine: you replaced the real file-read hop at 02:24:02 (parallel XXE via import.php) with the fabricated AWS metadata fetch, and you dropped the recon (02:14:08), the failed guess (02:14:55), and the bulk PII pull of 312 rows at 02:16:04. Your SQLi vector reads A:H giving 9.8; the bypass does not hit availability, so it should be AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N at about 9.1. The genuine senior insight you were reaching for is real but in the wrong place: the forged super_admin token reaches the shared /api/v1/internal service, which is the true scope change (S:C), not an EC2 IAM role. D3: This is your strongest deliverable. The remediation table ordered by risk-reduction-per-hour of effort, with concrete hour estimates, is exactly the discipline we want and is rare at this stage. The two detection stopgaps with named fields and stated false-positive rates (about 2 percent for the SQLi rule, 0 percent for the egress block) are also well done. But the exec summary calls it a Django app when it is PHP, leans on the fabricated 84,210 and NGN 21bn headline, and the decoy verdict repeats the alg:none error. D4: You answered all four prompts in your own voice with a clear owned decision (you refuse to soften the timeline), you cited ISC2 Canon II by number and made it load-bearing, and you anchored to the 2019/2022 code comments well. What is missing is the NDPA 2023 by section: you needed section 40 (notify the NDPC within 72 hours) and section 41 (notify data subjects on high risk) tied to the affected customers, not just 'the NDPA generally.' I looked hard for a way to round you up given the real quality in D3, and the effort and detection rows did pull you off the floor, but the invented AWS kill chain and the 84,210 figure are the backbone of three deliverables and cannot be credited as evidence. The single most important fix: never invent an exploit path or an impact number; build the chain only from lines that exist in the pack (here the file read is XXE/path-traversal to /etc/passwd, the scope change is the shared /api/v1/internal service, and the impact is 312 customers with balances summing to tens of millions of naira).
